key_insight: Ensemble Kalman Inversion can automatically tune a 16-parameter spectral eddy-viscosity closure so coarse LES spectra better match DNS in forced 2D turbulence.
engineering_relevance: This offers a derivative-free way to calibrate turbulence models online, improving LES fidelity without hand-tuning closure coefficients.
method: Parameterize the subgrid closure as a wavenumber-dependent spectral viscosity with 16 parameters.
Run an ensemble of coarse LES simulations and compare their kinetic energy spectra to filtered DNS data.
Iteratively update the parameters with ensemble statistics to reduce spectral mismatch.
evidence_signal: Performance is evaluated by how well the calibrated LES reproduces the DNS kinetic energy spectrum over the LES-resolved wavenumber range, with convergence of the spectral mismatch used as the main indicator.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated for forced two-dimensional turbulence, so transferability to 3D, different flows, or out-of-sample regimes still needs validation.
paper_title: Online Learning of a Spectral Eddy Viscosity Closure for Large Eddy Simulation Using Ensemble Kalman Inversion
